text:
clare: Quick check-in on private deployment networking defaults. We need a single GA default path + clear migration/rollback semantics. Options: shared relay (fast), customer-egress (static IPs), peering (BGP). Please call out what we ship first and how ops/CS safely move customers later.

noah: My leaning is shared relay for GA. Minimal customer setup, works for 90% of new installs. Key ask: document IP pool limits, per-tenant egress quotas, and chargeback model.

tor: Relay OK, but we must avoid "silent failures" when customers expect their own IPs. Need console flags showing current mode + last validation result. Also require an operator-level override to prevent auto-fallback for high-trust customers.

netops-ivy: Peering isn't a GA default (contracts/ASN/engineering effort). Suggest: default=relay, opt-in=customer-egress (self-serve), peering=enterprise-only via Sales. For peering, include a gating checklist (ASN, prefix filters, ACLs, test plan).

cs-ravi: Field note: customers ask for "static egress IPs" and audit logs. For customer-egress opt-in, add a signed token verification flow (we give a URL and token they must curl from their NAT to prove ownership).

clare: Proposed behavior: - Default mode: relay - Customer-egress: self-serve opt-in (validate IP ownership, optional reverse DNS check) - Peering: gated Dedicated feature - Fallback: agent runs health probes; after N=3 consecutive failures, auto-fallback to relay with audit event. Console shows last_probe, failure_count, and revert_reason.

noah: API sketch for switch + dry-run:
```
POST /v1/tenants/:tid/connectivity
{ "mode": "relay|egress|peering", "egress_ips": ["198.51.100.10"], "asn": "64520" }

POST /v1/tenants/:tid/connectivity/validate
{ "mode": "egress", "egress_ips": ["198.51.100.10"] }
# returns { "ok": true, "problems": [] }
```
Add GET /v1/tenants/:tid/connectivity/status -> {"mode":"egress","health":"ok","last_probe":".."} (display-only).

tor: Migration semantics: drain active sockets, steer new connections to target path, warm KV cache for 60s after cutover. Rollback triggers: error_rate delta > 1% OR 99th latency increases > 50ms sustained for 2 mins. On rollback re-run automatic cleanup and surface why. QA to create a reproducible failover harness.

netops-ivy: IPv6: we must accept IPv6-only egress from customers. If customer-egress provides IPv6-only, validate upstream reachability and document NAT64 limitations. Relay should support NAT64 conversion or provide IPv6 egress path. Add this to the packaging checklist.

cs-ravi: Add communication templates to CS playbook: pre-cutover checklist, test URLs, expected downtime (should be none), rollback notice. Also include outbound traffic policy: customers must only use egress for app traffic not arbitrary tunneling.

clare: Acceptance criteria for GA (proposal):
- Relay default: onboarding template works end-to-end with minimal firewall changes
- Customer-egress self-serve: validation endpoint + signed-token ownership proof
- Console: per-tenant mode + last_probe + revert_reason visible
- Auto-fallback: 3 consecutive probe failures -> revert to relay + audit log entry
- Migration safety: drain/warm/threshold-based auto-revert implemented and smoke-tested
- Documentation: Packaging checklist + CS templates + IPv6 guidance

infra-bot: infra-bot: Draft uploaded: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/private-connectivity-readiness (comments enabled) :robot_face:

noah: Action items: I -> relay capacity & cost model, Tor -> migration smoke test and thresholds, Ivy -> peering gating checklist and IPv6 notes, Ravi -> CS templates. Clare -> update roadmap ticket and mark GA gate with the acceptance criteria above.

clare: One more: include an operator-only flag to disable auto-fallback per-tenant (for customers that accept risk). That should be audit-logged.

(ended)
